# LLM Token Budgeting and Context Management

How to manage token budgets, context windows, and costs in multi-agent LLM
systems — with citation-backed evidence from 61 sources including 12 academic
papers.

## Key Finding

Context windows are smaller than advertised (effective: 60-70% of maximum [45]),
performance degrades 13.9%-85% even with perfect retrieval [6], and multi-agent
costs compound multiplicatively ($2,250/day for 3 agents with fan-out [23]).
Prevention (memory pointers, programmatic tool calling) beats recovery
(summarization, truncation) at every level.

## Decision Framework

| Problem | Solution | Expected Savings |
|---------|----------|-----------------|
| Large tool outputs fill context | Memory pointers [5] | Up to 99.99% token reduction |
| Multi-step tool workflows | Programmatic tool calling [22] | 37% token reduction |
| Repetitive prompt prefixes | Prompt caching [17] | 90% on reads |
| Per-agent cost overruns | Agent Contracts [1] + 3-layer governance [23] | 70-90% |
| Cross-session memory needed | LangGraph checkpoints + Mem0 [20][52] | 26% accuracy gain |
| Context quality degradation | 80% fill ceiling + observation masking [13][56] | Prevents failures |
| Multi-provider cost optimization | OpenRouter routing + model tiering [18] | 30-85% |

## Quick Start

1. **Set a context ceiling**: Use 80% of advertised window as soft limit
2. **Enable prompt caching**: 90% savings on cached reads with Anthropic
3. **Add memory pointers**: Keep tool outputs >5K tokens out of context
4. **Track costs**: Langfuse (open source) or LiteLLM for per-agent attribution
5. **Enforce budgets**: Per-agent limits with graduated throttling (80%→95%→100%)
